A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C. Their methods, theoretical results and experiments can be reliably matched despite reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C report original navigation simulations on Luxembourg and Monaco road networks, including algorithm comparisons, parameter sensitivity and exploration visualizations.

after.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C retain original navigation experiments, including five-run algorithm comparisons and lengthscale sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the GP-UCB/GP-BUCB/GP-TS selection rules, combined graph and feature kernel, rectification procedure and SVGP optimization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate simulated energy-efficient navigation on the same Luxembourg and Monaco networks, with routes A and B in each. Context features and the represented navigation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains GP-UCB, GP-BUCB and GP-TS alongside BI-UCB, BI-BUCB and BI-TS. The comparator sets in the parametrization and lengthscale experiments also remain unchanged; newly cited methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated GP variance from 0.25^2 sigma_det to 0.25^2 sigma_det^2, and noise variance from 0.1^2 sigma_det to 0.1^2 sigma_det^2, where sigma_det denotes standard deviation. This revises the reported simulation settings, but the PDFs do not establish reruns. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The confidence-parameter comparison, lengthscale sensitivity analysis and route-exploration visualizations are retained. Removing v2's standalone Luxembourg A lengthscale figure does not remove an analysis: those results remain in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report five evaluations per experimental configuration and retain the same mean and standard-error reporting. No repeated-run count, seed information or statistical testing procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The reported experimental curves, uncertainty regions and route visualizations are retained across Figures 2–3 and Appendix C. The results displayed in v2 Figure 4 remain in v3 Figure 5. The revised variance description is not accompanied by changed reported outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.2 and 3.6, Assumptions 3.3–3.4, the lemmas and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The added comparisons with existing bounds provide interpretation rather than a new formal result or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: Bayesian regret bounds for the three GP algorithms, the claimed first GP-BayesUCB bound, and a contextual combinatorial framework for energy-efficient navigation.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds an explanation of the finite per-round arm restriction. Section 3.1 expands discussion of possible gaps in dependence on K and tightness in T, explicitly distinguishing unavailable general Bayesian lower bounds from cited non-Bayesian bounds.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the documented variance scaling used to specify the GP environment and observation noise. Appendix B's kernel implementation, route endpoints, optimizer rates, batch size and inducing-point count remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wen et al. (2015), Merlis and Mannor (2020), Scarlett (2018), and Cai and Scarlett (2021) to contextualize bound dependence and possible optimality gaps. Table 1 also gains explicit regret-rate comparisons. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds limited explanatory passages, consolidates author and affiliation information, removes the keyword line and makes small wording edits. The main section sequence and organization of Appendices A–C remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide ICLR reformatting changes margins, typography, title and author layout, and figure placement and sizing. Table 1 gains a regret row and expanded caption; Figure 3 uses a more compact arrangement with shared labeling. The redundant main-text lengthscale figure is removed while its appendix counterpart is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the dimensionally inconsistent variance specification in Section 4.1 and makes theoretical scope and possible bound gaps clearer through Sections 2.1 and 3.1 and Table 1. These improve clarity and reproducibility without changing the proofs or empirical evidence. The added non-Bayesian lower-bound comparison remains suggestive rather than establishing Bayesian optimality.
